item.title: Command palette error state persists after branch name conflict
item.body: ## Bug report: Command palette error state persists after branch name conflict ### Description When creating a new Git branch via the command palette (Cmd+Shift+P) using a name that already exists as a local branch, Trae correctly shows an error state (red outline on the input). However, after resolving the conflict (e.g. choosing a different, valid branch name), the command palette remains in the error state for subsequent commands. The red error outline persists even when running unrelated commands later. This makes it look like every command is failing, even when they succeed. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open Trae IDE on a Git-enabled project. 2. Open the command palette with `Cmd+Shift+P`. 3. Run the command to create a new Git branch. 4. Enter a branch name that already exists locally. 5. Observe the input shows an error state (red outline) indicating the name conflict. 6. Close the palette or cancel the command. 7. Reopen the command palette (`Cmd+Shift+P`). ### Expected behavior - The error state (red outline) should be cleared once: - The invalid action is cancelled, or - A new valid command runs successfully. - Subsequent uses of the command palette should start in a neutral (non-error) state. ### Actual behavior - The error state (red outline) persists in the command palette input even after: - The initial branch name conflict is resolved, and - Subsequent commands run successfully. - The palette visually appears to be in an error state for all commands until Trae IDE is reloaded (or the session is otherwise reset). ### Impact - Confusing UX: it looks like later commands are failing even when they succeed. - Reduces trust in the command palette feedback, especially around Git operations. ### Environment - IDE: Trae IDE (version: unknown, latest available at the time of report) - OS: macOS - Git: local repository with at least one existing branch that can be used to trigger the name conflict ### Suggested fix (optional) - Ensure the command palette input error state is reset: - When the user cancels the command, or - After a command successfully completes, or - When the palette is reopened.
